title: Rank invariance of the 3D Stokes solve on ParMesh: 1 vs 4 vs 16 ranks (direct path)
physics: the T1 identity field (u = curl A and p = P, both O(1), mu = 0.37), sym form, the same fixed discrete problem on 1, 4 and 16 MPI ranks (one node, fluids_mpi.launch): octant Kuhn N = 16 with Dirichlet data on all six faces, and (amendment TD1) octant Kuhn N = 4 with Dirichlet on x0, y0, z0 and the exact traction on x1, y1, z1

element.geometry: affine (cube, duct); isoparametric P2/Q2 with the fixed nodes (sphere)

mixed_variant.data: the same field file (mms_data): nodal Dirichlet data of u on x0, y0, z0; traction g = f1c_stokes_check.Field.traction('sym', x, n), the exact sigma_sym n of the field, on x1, y1, z1 (the T2 convention); sym form, mu = 0.37, f = the field's forcing
mixed_variant.why: With all six faces Dirichlet and MFEM's ownership (a shared DOF belongs to the lowest rank of its group) every boundary DOF's owner holds a boundary element containing it on the METIS partitions of N = 16 (and of every mesh and rank count probed, 220 combinations), so 'essential DOFs only from the rank's own boundary elements' loses none; with a PARTIAL Dirichlet set it does (Kuhn N = 4, x0 y0 z0: 3 of 651 DOFs at 4 ranks, 39 at 16). The all-Dirichlet problem therefore cannot tell the two essential-DOF rules apart

parameters.comparison: every rank count's Evaluators cover each fixed element id exactly once; the solutions are compared at the fixed quadrature points by element id (difference_sums); both problems (all-Dirichlet N = 16, mixed N = 4) are run on 1, 4 and 16 ranks and every item below is the worst over both
